attribution: Kristen Browne and Heidi Schlehlein (2023), 3D Reference Organ Set for Female v1.5, HuBMAP / Human Reference Atlas. DOI: 10.48539/HBM352.BTSQ.586. CC BY 4.0.
modifications: Selected original female pelvic/reproductive/urinary/digestive/bony and associated vascular meshes from a single official united GLB; original positions, topology and node identities retained; neutral material for app coloring; normalized normals and 18-bit Draco position quantization. No inferred anatomy, no registration to male datasets, no scan volumes.

coordinates.sourceToApp: Identity: original GLB POSITION coordinates are retained; all source nodes have no matrix/TRS transforms. Common relative positions are inherited from one united HRA female reference model.
coordinates.orientationEvidence: Left ovary has greater X than right ovary; urinary bladder is anterior (+Z) to rectum/sacrum; fundus is superior (+Y) to cervix/vagina. Source GLB is Y-up, metre convention. No per-organ translation, scale, rotation or registration has been applied.

limitations: A pelvic subset of the HRA reference female, not a complete female musculoskeletal body.
A separate urethra mesh is absent; urinary bladder neck and ureteral orifices are preserved with their original identities and are not relabeled as urethra.
No pelvic-floor muscle, external genitalia or anal-canal mesh is added where absent in the selected source.
Named meshes include anatomical surface/region subdivisions (e.g. uterine walls, ostia, pouch surface) and are not all separately dissectible solid organs.

Source labels/ontology references are retained; some generic labels (e.g. pelvic bone tissue or bladder fundus) are disambiguated for display using the original node name. The superior rectal vein has an upstream copied artery label/ontology: display name follows source vein hierarchy/material, and conflicting normalized ontology fields are cleared. The archived per-organ uterus description contains an apparent Male/Female template error; dataset provenance here follows the united-female record.
The combined HRA reference model contains organ models from a curated atlas; do not imply every geometry represents a single patient segmentation.
Use as its own dataset. It is not spatially registered to Z-Anatomy or BodyParts3D.

coverage.ligaments: broad, round, cardinal, uterosacral, ovarian, suspensory; mesosalpinx and mesovarium
